questions.question: How do Shapley values attribute feature importance?
questions.reference_answer: Shapley values use cooperative game theory to determine a feature's influence on a prediction. A Shapley value is calculated by averaging a feature's marginal contributions across all possible orderings of features. The efficiency property means the entire prediction equals the sum of the Shapley values of individual features.

questions.question: Who published the Shapley value technique and when?
questions.reference_answer: Lloyd Shapley published the technique in 1951, and it contributed to his 2012 Nobel prize in Economics.

questions.question: What is the Q-learning update rule?
questions.reference_answer: Q-learning is an implementation of TD learning that made it easier to prove convergence. The update is an online update rule for the action-value function, which you iterate to refine.

questions.question: What problem does Double Q-learning solve?
questions.reference_answer: A bad initial update can create a loop where the agent keeps making suboptimal decisions. Double Q-learning solves this by using two action-value functions.

questions.question: What is Speedy Q-learning?
questions.reference_answer: Speedy Q-learning is like eligibility traces but implemented differently: it updates the action-value function by exponentially decaying a sum of the previous and current TD update.

questions.question: How does DQN update the Q-value?
questions.reference_answer: The DQN update rule is like Q-learning, but the Q-value is approximated by a function, and that function has a set of parameters.

questions.question: What are the main hyperparameter tuning strategies?
questions.reference_answer: The three main strategies are grid search, random search, and Bayesian search. For all three, the first step is the same: select a range of candidate values.

questions.question: How do you get a score function for hyperparameter tuning in scikit-learn?
questions.reference_answer: Hyperparameter tuning methods in scikit-learn are set to use score functions; you can get one by taking the negative RMSE.

questions.question: How do you create a hyperparameter tuning job with the CREATE MODEL statement?
questions.reference_answer: The statement for creating a hyperparameter tuning job is very similar to the model creation statement, with key differences for hyperparameter tuning, and selects from the training data.

questions.question: Why should you consider deployment when choosing which model to train?
questions.reference_answer: The end goal of your model is to provide a valuable service to the people who use it, so when choosing which model to train you should always consider whether you will be able to deploy it.

questions.question: How do you validate that a deployed model keeps learning something useful?
questions.reference_answer: Track when the performance of the deployed model drifts; track the model's uncertainty or bring it back to the business and usage metrics.

questions.question: What is client-side deployment?
questions.reference_answer: Client-side deployment runs all computations on the client, eliminating the need for a server to run models — on computers, tablets, modern smartphones, and some connected devices.

questions.question: What is the goal of deploying a model?
questions.reference_answer: The goal of deploying a model is to allow users to interact with it.
